title: The Egyptian media: podcasts, documentaries, transcription and subtitles

blocks.text: The talk of the media is the richest source of authentic Egyptian: podcasts, documentaries, long interviews, popular videos. Compared to the dialogues of the course is faster, more disordered (pauses, repetitions, self-corrections, sentences left in half) and more mixed: English words in the podcasts of young people, fuṣḥā in the voice of the narrator and in the vocabulary of experts. In this unit learn the discursive signals that organize a story or reasoning, the rapid forms of quick speech, the conventions to transcribe the Egyptian into Arabic characters and the techniques to translate it into English, both in an integral translation and in subtitles. It's the Egyptian side of the translation form. Eight weeks, in parallel with the end of B2-13, B2-14 and B2-15.

rows: EGY-11 EGY-16 (in particular EGY-14, interviews, and EGY-16, the graphs); B2-13 in parallel
12–13 hours · eight weeks (weeks) 211–218), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, an Egyptian tutor, podcasts and authentic Egyptian videos chosen by the tutor, a program to slow down audio
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. follow 10–15 minutes of a podcast or an interview in Egyptian, understanding the main points and details
important;
2. recognize the discursive signals of the story and reasoning and their function;
3. understand the most frequent rapid forms of fast speech and adapted English words;
4. transcribe into Arabic characters one minute of Egyptian, faithful version and clean version;
5. translate the Egyptian spoken in English, in full version and in subtitles.
Eight-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

The method. 1) Listen to everything once without writing. 2) Divide audio into pieces of 10–15 seconds. 3) Write each piece, leaving empty spaces where you don't understand. 4) Listen only to empty spaces, even at reduced speed. 5) Read everything while you listen again. 6) If you can, have an Egyptian speaker check out the uncertain words. At the beginning one minute of audio requires 20–30 working minutes: it's normal.

The rhythm of the story. Those who tell in a podcast use the voice: elongates vowels for emphasis (kbīīīr Very large; wallāāāhi), slow down before the surprise (laʾ w-ēh...) and accelerates in the least important parts.
